Q: Extracting File Name from Path in Batch File A:

You can use %%~nf to get just the basename of the file without the extension.

There are other options listed in for /?:

%~I         - expands %I removing any surrounding quotes (")
%~fI        - expands %I to a fully qualified path name
%~dI        - expands %I to a drive letter only
%~pI        - expands %I to a path only
%~nI        - expands %I to a file name only
%~xI        - expands %I to a file extension only
%~sI        - expanded path contains short names only
%~aI        - expands %I to file attributes of file
%~tI        - expands %I to date/time of file
%~zI        - expands %I to size of file

Q: Making video from clips on moviepy only showing last image A:

from moviepy.editor import ImageClip, concatenate_videoclips

import os

images = [

"/mnt/data/a_polished_celebratory_school_group_photo_poster.png", 

"/mnt/data/a_polished_formal_school_farewell_poster_graphi.png", 

"/mnt/data/a_polished_celebratory_school_farewell_poster_p.png"

]

valid_images = [img for img in images if os.path.exists(img)]

clips = []

for img_path in valid_images:

clip = ImageClip(img_path).resize(height=720).set_duration(2) 

clips.append(clip)

final_video = concatenate_videoclips(clips, method="compose")

output_path = "/mnt/data/farewell_video.mp4"

final_video.write_videofile(

output_path, 

fps=12, 

codec="libx264", 

audio=False, 

preset="ultrafast"

)

print("Done:", output_path)

Q: How to detect app install source / deferred deep link on Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift) after web popup campaign login? A:

On Android, the official approach is usually the Google Play Install Referrer API combined with App Links/deep links. iOS is harder because Apple does not expose install referrer data directly, so most production apps rely on Universal Links + deferred deep linking providers (Branch, AppsFlyer, Adjust, etc.). Firebase Dynamic Links used to simplify this flow, but since deprecation many teams are moving toward custom routing or SDK-less alternatives.

Q: How to clear a single-select slicer A:

It looks like the post you referenced was made about three years ago. It might not take into account the new slicer visuals that are now included with Power BI Desktop by default.

New slicer options

These new slicers include an eraser icon that allows the user to clear all selections from the visual. In order for the user to access this functionality, the Force Selection option for the slicer must be disabled.
